text:
Git branching is a powerful tool in version control that helps teams work on different features without interfering with each other's code. Instead of everyone editing the main project directly, developers create separate feature branches. This keeps the main branch stable and ready to release at any time.

Once a feature is complete, the developer submits a pull request, which is a formal request to merge their changes back into the main branch. Teammates review the code, suggest improvements, and approve the merge if everything looks good. This workflow ensures quality and reduces conflicts, making collaboration smooth and organized even in large projects.
